author: Ben Pascoe

HMW DNA Extraction from Bacteria Using NEB Monarch HMW DNA Extraction Kit 🔧 Materials Required (Not Supplied) Microcentrifuge Thermal mixer (1.5 mL + 2 mL blocks) Vertical rotating mixer (e.g., HulaMixer) Ethanol ≥95% Cold PBS or TE/Tris Isopropanol (550 µL/sample or 275 µL low input) 1.5 mL DNase-free low DNA binding tubes Wide-bore pipette tips Lysozyme (Gram-neg: 25 mg/mL; Gram-pos: 10 mg/mL in STET) Additional lysis agents (e.g., lysostaphin if needed) 🧤 Preparation Clean bench with 80% ethanol. Wear PPE. Preheat thermal mixers to 37°C and 56°C. Add ethanol to gDNA Wash Buffer as per label. Chill PBS/TE/Tris buffer. Label tubes. Store Proteinase K and RNase A at -20°C. 🧫

▶️ Start Sequencing Run Use MinKNOW software. Choose appropriate flow cell and kit settings (e.g., LSK114). Set run time (e.g., 24–72 hours depending on goal). Start sequencing and monitor real-time QC metrics.

🧫 Sample Preparation Extract total DNA from microbial or environmental samples. Use a high-fidelity, contamination-free method (e.g., Qiagen PowerSoil for stool). Quantify DNA using Qubit (dsDNA HS). Normalize DNA to 10–50 ng per PCR reaction .

🧬 Hybrid Metagenomic Sequencing Protocol (Illumina + ONT) 📦 Sample Collection & DNA Extraction Collect samples (e.g. stool, soil, rumen, etc.) under sterile conditions. Store samples at −80°C if not processing within 1 hour. Extract high molecular weight (HMW) DNA using a suitable kit (e.g. QIAGEN MagAttract HMW DNA Kit). Minimise mechanical shearing. Aim for fragment sizes >20 kb for ONT compatibility. Quantify DNA with Qubit and assess quality on TapeStation or agarose gel.

🧬 C-SOP-1001: HMW DNA Extraction from Bacteria Using NEB Monarch HMW DNA Extraction Kit 🔧 Materials Required (Not Supplied) Microcentrifuge Thermal mixer (1.5 mL + 2 mL blocks) Vertical rotating mixer (e.g., HulaMixer) Ethanol ≥95% Cold PBS or TE/Tris Isopropanol (550 µL/sample or 275 µL low input) 1.5 mL DNase-free low DNA binding tubes Wide-bore pipette tips Lysozyme (Gram-neg: 25 mg/mL; Gram-pos: 10 mg/mL in STET) Additional lysis agents (e.g., lysostaphin if needed) 🧤 Preparation Clean bench with 80% ethanol. Wear PPE. Preheat thermal mixers to 37°C and 56°C. Add ethanol to gDNA Wash Buffer as per label. Chill PBS/TE/Tris buffer. Label tubes. Store Proteinase K and RNase A at -20°C. 🧫 Step 1: Cell Pellet Centrifuge bacterial culture at 12,000 × g for 1 min in a Monarch Pestle Tube. 🦠 Step 2: Lysis A. Gram-negative Bacteria Resuspend pellet in 300 µL cold PBS (150 µL for low input). Add 10 µL lysozyme (25 mg/mL) , vortex briefly. Add 300 µL HMW Lysis Buffer , invert 5–10×. Incubate at 37°C with agitation: 2000 rpm (faster lysis, shorter fragments) 500 rpm (slower lysis, longer fragments) Until lysate turns clear (~5 min) B. Gram-positive Bacteria Resuspend in STET buffer + lysozyme (10 mg/mL) . Incubate 30 min at 37°C (no agitation) . Add 300 µL HMW Lysis Buffer , invert 5–10×. 🔥 Step 3: Proteinase K Digestion Increase thermal mixer to 56°C if needed. Add 20 µL Proteinase K (10 µL for low input), invert 10–20×. Choose Homogenization: Thermal Mixer: Incubate 30 min at 56°C , 2000 rpm. Rotor-stator: Homogenize 5–15 sec, then incubate 30 min at 56°C . 💧 Step 4: RNA Removal Add 10 µL RNase A (5 µL for low input), invert 5–10×. Incubate 10 min at 56°C , same speed as lysis. 🧪 Step 5: Protein Separation Add 300 µL Protein Separation Solution , invert for 1 min or mix at 20 rpm. Centrifuge 10 min at 16,000 × g . Carefully transfer upper DNA phase (~800 µL) to new 2 mL tube. 🧬 Step 6: DNA Binding to Beads Add 2 DNA Capture Beads to tube. Add 550 µL isopropanol (275 µL low input). Mix gently: Rotate at 10 rpm for 5 min OR Invert 25–30× slowly (5–6 sec per inversion) Watch for visible DNA wrapping around beads 🚿 Step 7: Wash Steps Remove liquid carefully (avoid touching beads). Wash with 500 µL gDNA Wash Buffer , invert 2–3×, then remove. Repeat wash. 🧲 Step 8: Bead Transfer Transfer beads to Monarch Collection Tube II + bead retainer . Pulse spin (≤1 sec). Move beads to a fresh 2 mL tube . Insert bead retainer into 1.5 mL DNA low-bind tube . 💦 Step 9: Elution Add 100 µL Elution Buffer II (≥5 min at 56°C, 300 rpm). Optional: use 50 µL with more frequent gentle shaking Pour eluate + beads into bead retainer in 1.5 mL tube. 🌀 Step 10: Final Handling Centrifuge 30 sec at 12,000 × g . Discard beads and retainer. Pipette eluate 5–10× with wide-bore tips to disperse aggregates. Dissolve DNA: 1 h at 37°C , or 24 h at RT , or Overnight at 4°C Pipette again before use. 📦 Storage Short-term: 4°C Long-term: -20°C (in Elution Buffer: 10 mM Tris, pH 9.0, 0.5 mM EDTA) 📚 Additional Resources UHMW DNA Extraction for Ultra-Long Read Nanopore UHMW DNA Cleanup Protocol

🧬 Hybrid Metagenomic Sequencing Protocol (Illumina + ONT) 📦 Sample Collection & DNA Extraction Collect samples (e.g. stool, soil, rumen, etc.) under sterile conditions. Store samples at −80°C if not processing within 1 hour. Extract high molecular weight (HMW) DNA using a suitable kit (e.g. QIAGEN MagAttract HMW DNA Kit). Minimise mechanical shearing. Aim for fragment sizes >20 kb for ONT compatibility. Quantify DNA with Qubit and assess quality on TapeStation or agarose gel.

steps.title: Prepare workspace and reagents
steps.instruction: Clean the work area with 80 % ethanol, wear appropriate PPE and follow local GLP guidelines. Set up an ice bucket for temporary reagent/sample storage. Thaw Illumina HT1 buffer at room temperature and keep it on ice (store at 2–8 °C after thaw). Prepare 0.2 N NaOH by mixing 200 µL of 1.0 N NaOH with 800 µL nuclease‑free water; use within 8 h.

steps.title: Thaw reagent cartridge
steps.instruction: Two hours before the run, remove the Nextera XT reagent cartridge from –20 °C storage. Submerge only the base in a room‑temperature water bath (do not exceed the line indicated). Thaw for ~1.5 h for v3 kits or ~1 h for v2 kits. Dry the base and invert the cartridge 10 times to mix reagents. Verify that positions 1, 2, and 4 are fully thawed with no precipitate, then keep the cartridge at 4 °C until loading.

steps.title: Initialize MiSeq instrument
steps.instruction: Power on the MiSeq (switch on the back). Log in to BaseSpace if the instrument is networked. Wait for the MiSeq Control Software (MCS) to finish initializing.

steps.title: Denature and dilute DNA library
steps.instruction: In a clean tube combine 5 µL of 4 nM DNA library with 5 µL 0.2 N NaOH, vortex 10 s and spin 1 min. Incubate 5 min at room temperature. Add 990 µL chilled HT1 buffer to obtain a 20 pM denatured library, then dilute to the final loading concentration (e.g., 10 pM).

steps.title: Denature and dilute PhiX (optional spike‑in)
steps.instruction: Prepare a 4 nM PhiX stock by mixing 2 µL 10 nM PhiX with 3 µL Tris‑Cl/Tween. Then combine 5 µL 4 nM PhiX with 5 µL 0.2 N NaOH, vortex 10 s, spin 1 min, incubate 5 min, and add 990 µL HT1 to reach 20 pM PhiX. For v2 kits, mix 375 µL PhiX with 225 µL HT1 to obtain 12.5 pM. Add 1–5 % PhiX to the final sample pool depending on library complexity.

steps.title: Setup MiSeq run parameters
steps.instruction: Ensure at least 100 GB of free disk space. In MCS → Run Options enable “Replicate analysis locally”. Create a Sample Sheet using Illumina Experiment Manager (IEM) and load it into the instrument.

steps.title: Prepare and load flow cell
steps.instruction: Retrieve the flow cell and PR2 buffer from 4 °C storage. Rinse the flow cell with laboratory‑grade water, dry with lint‑free lens paper, and wipe the glass with an ethanol‑wetted lens tissue. Install the flow cell into the clamp and wait for RFID recognition.

steps.title: Load incorporation buffer (PR2) and waste bottle
steps.instruction: Raise the sipper handle, load the mixed PR2 buffer bottle and confirm RFID detection. Empty the waste bottle, replace it, then lower the sipper so it contacts both the PR2 buffer and waste bottle.

steps.title: Load denatured DNA library into cartridge
steps.instruction: Tap the reagent cartridge to gather its contents. Pierce the foil at the “Load Sample” port. Pipette 600 µL of the denatured library into the well, then tap gently to settle the sample at the base of the well.

steps.title: Insert cartridge into MiSeq
steps.instruction: When prompted “Load Reagent Cartridge”, remove the wash tray and dry the chiller base if needed. Insert the cartridge (Illumina label facing out) until fully seated and confirm that the RFID is read.

steps.title: Confirm sample sheet
steps.instruction: MCS will automatically look for a matching barcode sample sheet. If not found, manually browse to select the correct sheet, then click “Save and Continue” → “Next”.

steps.title: Start sequencing run
steps.instruction: Review experiment name, workflow, and read length. Run the Pre‑run Check; when all checks pass, click “Start Run”.

steps.title: Post‑run wash
steps.instruction: Follow on‑screen prompts to load the wash tray, wash bottle, and optionally the MiSeq wash tube (0.01 % NaOCl). Start the wash. Do not remove the flow cell or wash tray during the wash. Leave the wash solution in the tray/bottle after completion.

steps.title: Monitor sequencing run
steps.instruction: Use the Sequencing screen (view‑only) or BaseSpace/SAV to monitor cycles, cluster intensities, and quality scores throughout the run.

steps.title: Export sequencing data
steps.instruction: Navigate to D:\Illumina\MiSeq Output\Run Folder\Data\Intensities\BaseCalls and download the fastq.gz files for R1 and R2, or retrieve them via BaseSpace or a local network share.

steps.title: Instrument shutdown or reboot
steps.instruction: For a weekly reboot: MCS → Manage Instrument → Reboot. For shutdown: MCS → Manage Instrument → Shutdown, then turn off the power switch, wait 10 min, and power on again.

steps.title: Monthly maintenance (brief)
steps.instruction: Perform post‑run bleach (PTL) and other cleaning steps as described in the MiSeq System Guide.

steps.title: Nextera XT library preparation – tagmentation
steps.instruction: In a PCR plate combine 10 µL TD (tagmentation buffer) with 5 µL genomic DNA (0.2 ng/µL). Add 5 µL ATM, vortex, spin 280 × g for 1 min, then run the thermal cycler at 55 °C for 5 min, hold at 10 °C. Add 5 µL NT, mix, spin, and incubate at room temperature for 5 min.

steps.title: Nextera XT library preparation – amplification
steps.instruction: Add i7 and i5 indices (5 µL each) to the tagmented DNA, then add 15 µL NPM. Spin briefly and run PCR: 72 °C 3 min → 95 °C 30 s → 12 cycles of 95 °C 10 s, 55 °C 30 s, 72 °C 30 s → final extension 72 °C 5 min → hold at 10 °C. After PCR, store at 2–8 °C for 2 days or overnight.

steps.title: Clean‑up libraries (AMPure XP)
steps.instruction: Transfer 50 µL PCR product to a new plate. Add 30 µL AMPure XP beads, shake at 1800 rpm for 2 min, incubate 5 min at room temperature, place on magnetic stand, and remove supernatant. Wash beads twice with 200 µL 80 % ethanol, remove residual ethanol, air‑dry 15 min, then elute in 52.5 µL RSB. Shake, incubate, magnet, and transfer 50 µL eluate to a new plate. Store at –25 °C to –15 °C for up to 7 days.

steps.title: Optional library quality check
steps.instruction: Run 1 µL of each library on an Agilent Bioanalyzer High‑Sensitivity DNA chip.

steps.title: Normalize libraries
steps.instruction: Transfer 20 µL of each library to a new plate. Prepare normalization mix: 4.4 mL LNA1 + 800 µL LNB1. Add 45 µL of this mix to each well, shake at 1800 rpm for 30 min, magnet, and discard supernatant. Wash twice with 45 µL LNW1, add 30 µL 0.1 N NaOH, shake 5 min, add 30 µL LNS1 to a new SGP plate, resuspend beads, shake 5 min, magnet, and transfer normalized library to the SGP plate. Spin at 1000 × g for 1 min. Store at –25 °C to –15 °C for up to 7 days.

steps.title: Pool normalized libraries
steps.instruction: Spin the SGP plate, transfer 5 µL from each sample to a PCR tube strip, pool all into a single tube (PAL), dilute to the desired loading concentration, and store PAL and SGP plates at –25 °C to –15 °C (up to 7 days).

steps.title: Denature and dilute pooled libraries for MiSeq
steps.instruction: Thaw HT1 buffer at room temperature and keep at 2–8 °C. For each library, combine 6 µL library with 594 µL HT1 (XT kit) or 24 µL library with 576 µL HT1 (other kits). Vortex, spin, incubate at 98 °C for 2 min, then place on ice for 5 min to obtain the final loading concentration.

steps.title: Campylobacter DNA extraction – culture
steps.instruction: Streak Campylobacter isolates onto chocolate, blood, or Brucella agar and incubate at 42 °C for 48 h. Using a sterile loop, harvest at least one loop‑full of growth and resuspend cells in 180 µL Buffer ATL. Incubate at 37 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Cell lysis and protein digestion
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL Proteinase K (from the kit) to the lysate, vortex, and incubate at 56 °C for 30–60 min. Briefly spin down condensation from the tube lid.

steps.title: RNase treatment and lysis enhancement
steps.instruction: Add 4 µL RNase (100 mg/mL) and 200 µL Buffer AL, vortex thoroughly, and incubate at 70 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: DNA binding
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of 95–100 % ethanol to the lysate, vortex, and transfer the entire volume (~600 µL) to a QIAamp spin column placed in a 2 mL collection tube. Centrifuge at 8000 rpm for 1 min at room temperature, discard flow‑through, and move the column to a clean 2 mL collection tube.

steps.title: Wash steps
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Buffer AW1, centrifuge 8000 rpm for 1 min at RT, discard flow‑through. Add 500 µL Buffer AW2, centrifuge at 14 000 rpm for 3 min to dry the membrane.

steps.title: DNA elution
steps.instruction: Place the column into a clean 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, add 50 µL Buffer AE (or nuclease‑free water) directly onto the membrane, let sit 1 min at RT, then centrifuge at 8000 rpm for 1 min to elute DNA. Store eluate at 4 °C short‑term or –20 °C long‑term.

steps.title: ONT Rapid Barcoding – reaction setup
steps.instruction: For each sample combine 2.5 µL Rapid Barcoding (RB) reagent, ≤2.5 µL genomic DNA (10–50 ng in ≤2.5 µL nuclease‑free water), and 0.5 µL barcode (BCXX) for a total volume of 5.5 µL. Mix by gentle flicking or pipetting.

steps.title: ONT Rapid Barcoding – incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the reaction at 30 °C for 1 min, then at 80 °C for 1 min. Immediately place on ice.

steps.title: Pooling and bead cleanup (Rapid Barcoding)
steps.instruction: Pool 2 µL from each barcoded sample into a single tube (total ≤10 µL). Add 1.8× volume of AMPure XP beads, incubate 5 min at RT, place on magnet 5 min, wash twice with 70 % ethanol, and elute in 10 µL elution buffer or nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Adapter ligation (Rapid Barcoding)
steps.instruction: To the 10 µL barcoded DNA add 1.0 µL Rapid Adapter (RAP) for a total of 11 µL. Mix by flicking or pipetting, incubate at RT for 5 min, then proceed directly to loading.

steps.title: Load library onto ONT flow cell (Rapid Barcoding)
steps.instruction: Prime the flow cell according to the ONT Flow Cell Priming SOP. Prepare loading mix: 37.5 µL Sequencing Buffer (SQB), 25.5 µL Loading Beads (LB, mixed immediately before use), and 12 µL final library. Mix gently and load 75 µL into the SpotON port drop‑by‑drop, avoiding bubbles. Close ports and lid.

steps.title: ONT Ligation Sequencing (LSK114) – DNA repair & end‑prep
steps.instruction: Combine up to 48 µL DNA sample with 7 µL NEBNext FFPE DNA Repair Buffer, 3 µL NEBNext FFPE DNA Repair Mix, 3.5 µL NEBNext Ultra II End Prep Reaction Buffer, and 3 µL NEBNext Ultra II End Prep Enzyme Mix (total ≈64.5 µL). Mix gently, spin briefly, incubate 20 °C for 5 min then 65 °C for 5 min, and place on ice.

steps.title: AMPure XP cleanup (post‑repair)
steps.instruction: Add 1× volume of AMPure XP beads (e.g., 65 µL), incubate 5 min at RT, magnet 5 min, discard supernatant, wash twice with 200 µL 70 % ethanol, air‑dry beads 2 min (avoid over‑drying), and elute DNA in 61 µL nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Adapter ligation (LSK114)
steps.instruction: To the 61 µL eluted DNA add 25 µL 5× Quick T4 DNA Ligase Buffer, 10 µL Adapter Mix (AMX), and 5 µL Quick T4 DNA Ligase (total 100 µL). Mix by gentle flicking and incubate at RT for 10–15 min.

steps.title: Post‑ligation bead cleanup
steps.instruction: Add 0.4× volume of AMPure XP beads (~40 µL), incubate 5 min at RT, magnet 5 min, discard supernatant, wash twice with 250 µL Long Fragment Buffer (LFB), air‑dry beads ≤2 min, and elute final library in 15 µL Elution Buffer (EB).

steps.title: Flow cell priming (MinION/GridION)
steps.instruction: Thaw and mix Flush Buffer (FB) with Flush Tether (FLT) to make the priming mix. Open the SpotON and priming ports, remove ~20 µL from the priming port to release air, then slowly inject 800 µL priming mix via the priming port.

steps.title: Load LSK114 library onto flow cell
steps.instruction: Prepare loading mix: 37.5 µL Sequencing Buffer (SQB), 25.5 µL Loading Beads (LB, mixed immediately before use), and 12 µL final library (from step 9). Mix gently, then load 75 µL into the SpotON port drop‑by‑drop. Close ports and lid.

steps.title: Optional flow‑cell wash (post‑run)
steps.instruction: After sequencing, optionally wash and reuse the flow cell using the ONT Flow Cell Wash Kit (up to 2–3 reuses). Store any remaining library at –20 °C (avoid freeze‑thaw cycles).

steps.title: 16S rRNA ONT workflow – PCR product cleanup
steps.instruction: Clean each 16S amplicon with 1× AMPure XP beads: add beads, incubate 5 min at RT, magnet, wash twice with 70 % ethanol, and elute in 10 µL nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: 16S library pooling and quantification
steps.instruction: Pool 10 µL of each barcoded amplicon, quantify the pool with Qubit, and aim for 50–200 fmol total DNA (up to 1 µg).

steps.title: 16S adapter ligation (if not pre‑tagged)
steps.instruction: Add 1.0 µL Rapid Adapter (RAP) or AMX to ~10 µL pooled amplicons (total ≈11 µL). Incubate 5 min at RT, then proceed to loading.

steps.title: Load 16S library onto ONT flow cell
steps.instruction: Prime the flow cell as per ONT Flow Cell Priming SOP. Prepare loading mix: ~12 µL DNA library, 25.5 µL Loading Beads (LB), and 37.5 µL Sequencing Buffer (SQB). Mix gently and load 75 µL drop‑wise onto the SpotON port.

steps.title: Start 16S sequencing run
steps.instruction: In MinKNOW select kit SQK‑16S024 (or latest), flow cell FLO‑MIN106D (R10.4.1 recommended), and run for 12–48 h depending on desired depth.

steps.title: Basecalling and taxonomic analysis
steps.instruction: Basecall reads using Guppy (or MinKNOW). Perform taxonomic classification with EPI2ME Fastq 16S workflow, or alternative tools such as QIIME 2, Kraken2, or NanoCLUST. Generate bar plots of relative abundances per sample.

steps.title: Store final libraries and flow cells
steps.instruction: Store final amplicon libraries at –20 °C (short‑term). Flow cells can be washed and reused 1–2 times.

description: 📝 Notes Ensure all reagents from the kit are at working temperature. Eluted DNA is suitable for downstream applications including PCR and sequencing. ✅ Notes Full-length 16S sequencing provides species-level resolution. Minimize chimera formation by using high-fidelity polymerases. Always run negative controls to detect contamination. 💡 Best Practices & Notes Aim for >40 Gbp of Illumina data per sample for deep profiling. ONT long reads help resolve repeats, rRNA operons, plasmids, and MGEs. For low-complexity samples, less sequencing depth may suffice. Optional: Use Hi-C or read cloud technologies for improved binning.
